children: U.S. apparel maker's fiscal Q2 revenue declined 2%, slightly missing analyst expectations
Adjusted EPS for fiscal Q2 rose year-over-year and beat analyst expectations
Company lowered full-year guidance due to softness at Lilly Pulitzer and macroeconomic pressures
Oxford Industries lowers fiscal 2026 net sales outlook to $1.43 bln-$1.47 bln
Company expects fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.60-$2.00, down from $2.11 in fiscal 2025
Oxford Industries sees Q3 net sales of $280 mln-$300 mln, adjusted loss per share of $1.40-$1.20
TARIFF REFUNDS - Gross margin benefited from $42 mln in tariff refund claims recognized as a reduction of cost of goods sold
LILLY PULITZER SOFTNESS - Sales declines at Lilly Pulitzer attributed to product and marketing challenges, per CEO Tom Chubb
MACROECONOMIC PRESSURE - Company cited ongoing macroeconomic consumer pressure as contributing to lower guidance
*Applies to a deviation of less than 1%; not applicable for per-share numbers.
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "hold" and the breakdown of recommendations is no "strong buy" or "buy", 6 "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the apparel & accessories peer group is "buy."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Oxford Industries Inc is $40.00, about 6% above its September 2 closing price of $37.74
The stock recently traded at 14 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 17 three months ago
